safety_health_committee_001.answer: yes. Committee: Faculty Steering Committee. Membership: 5-10 teachers elected by secret ballot. Issue scope: student discipline, faculty meetings, school rules, and health and safety items. Complaint process: Teachers report hazards to the principal.
safety_health_committee_001.evidence: "The steering committee may be established in a school for considering various areas such as, but not limited to, student discipline, faculty meetings, school rules, and health and safety items." (Page 8) "Teachers will report any health or safety hazards to the principal." (Page 16)
safety_health_committee_001.coder_notes: Updated evidence to include the clause on reporting health/safety hazards to the principal (Page 16), as the original evidence only covered the committee's scope and missed the complaint process mentioned in the answer.

safety_assault_protection_002.evidence: "In any case of intimidation, assault, battery, abuse, or threat with bodily harm by an individual or group upon a teacher in the course of his/her assigned duties, the Board shall provide legal counsel to advise the teacher of his/her rights and obligations with respect to such intimidation, assault, battery, abuse or bodily harm, and shall promptly render assistance necessary to the teacher in connection with handling of the incident by law enforcement and judicial authorities. Teachers shall immediately report any such incidents to their principal." (Page 35) "When an employee is assaulted or battered while in the line of duty, the work site shall maintain a record of the incident. The work site shall provide a copy of all School District reports to the employee as soon as possible. It is the employee's right to notify law enforcement and pursue charges as provided under Florida law." (Page 35)
safety_assault_protection_002.coder_notes: Replaced evidence from 9.03-1 (use of reasonable force) with 9.10 and 9.10-1, which directly address assault protections, legal counsel, reporting procedures, and post-assault record-keeping as requested by the question.

safety_student_discipline_003.evidence: 9.03 Student Discipline The teacher shall make every effort to deter misbehavior prior to sending a student to the office; however, a teacher may temporarily exclude a student from class by sending the student to the principal's office when the grossness of the offense, the persistence of the misbehavior, or the disruptive effect of the behavior makes the continued presence of the student in the classroom intolerable.

safety_remove_student_004.evidence: a teacher may temporarily exclude a student from class by sending the student to the principal's office when the grossness of the offense, the persistence of the misbehavior, or the disruptive effect of the behavior makes the continued presence of the student in the classroom intolerable.

safety_environment_006.answer: yes. Standards/Responsibility: Board keeps instructional rooms clean/free from hazards; principal maintains heating/cooling; custodial staff cleans lounges regularly. Priority given to rectify poor indoor air quality/mold. Complaint process: Teachers report hazards to principal.
safety_environment_006.evidence: The Board will keep all rooms, which are used for instructional purposes or preparation, clean and free from health and safety hazards. Each principal will take necessary steps to maintain the heating and cooling systems. Priority will be given to rectify schools with documented poor indoor air quality including mold. Teachers will report any health or safety hazards to the principal.
